record.context_brief: Anytime acceleration for gradient descent on smooth convex objectives
record.original_question: Consider gradient descent on a convex function f: R^d -> R that is L-smooth, meaning that its gradient exists and is L-Lipschitz. Starting from an initial point x0 in R^d, the iterates are defined by x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t), and f* = inf f with x* denoting a minimizer. What is the best anytime convergence rate for the individual-iterate error f(x_T) - f* that can be guaranteed uniformly over all such objectives by choosing a stepsize sequence (eta_t)_{t=0}^infinity? In particular, does there exist a stepsize sequence and an exponent alpha > 1 such that, for every horizon T in N and every L-smooth convex function f, the error f(x_T) - f* is bounded up to a universal constant factor by L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha, with the guarantee available in an anytime, monotonically decreasing form across all T?

evidence.quote: Given a convex function f : R^d -> R which is L-smooth (i.e. nabla f exists and is L-Lipschitz), and an initial point x0 in R^d, the GD iterates with stepsizes (eta_t)^infinity_{t=0} are defined as x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t nabla f(x_t).

Open Problem 1 What is the best anytime convergence rate achievable by GD with some stepsize sequence (eta_t)^infinity_{t=0}, uniformly over L-smooth convex functions? In particular, is there any stepsize sequence and some alpha > 1, such that for all L-smooth convex f, f(x_T) - f* . L ||x0 - x*||^2 / T^alpha for all T in N?
We remark that we seek an anytime, monotonically decreasing upper bound on the error: Indeed, with long steps, the errors themselves may not decrease monotonically.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f: R^d → R be a convex function that is L-smooth, i.e., differentiable with an L-Lipschitz gradient, and assume f attains its infimum f* = inf f at some minimizer x*. Fix an initial point x_0 ∈ R^d. Given a deterministic stepsize sequence (η_t)_{t=0}^∞ ⊂ (0, ∞) (chosen in advance, independently of f and of any stopping time), define the gradient descent iterates

    x_{t+1} = x_t − η_t ∇f(x_t),  t = 0, 1, 2, … .

Determine the best anytime convergence rate of the individual-iterate error f(x_T) − f* that can be guaranteed uniformly over all such (L, f, x_0). Specifically:

(a) Does there exist a stepsize sequence (η_t)_{t=0}^∞ and an exponent α > 1, together with a universal constant C > 0, such that for every L > 0, every L-smooth convex f: R^d → R with a minimizer x*, every x_0 ∈ R^d, and every horizon T ∈ N,

    f(x_T) − f* ≤ C · L ‖x_0 − x*‖^2 / T^α ?

(b) More generally, identify the largest exponent α (or, more finely, the optimal anytime function φ(T)) such that some stepsize sequence achieves f(x_T) − f* ≤ C · L ‖x_0 − x*‖^2 · φ(T) simultaneously for all T ∈ N, where the bound is required to be available in an anytime, monotonically decreasing form in T.
artifact.category_tag: Convex optimization / gradient descent stepsize schedules
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent work by Zhang and Jiang (2024/2025, "Anytime Acceleration of Gradient Descent") gives an affirmative answer to part (a): there is an explicit stepsize schedule based on the silver ratio achieving f(x_T) − f* ≤ O(L ‖x_0 − x*‖^2 / T^{1.119}) anytime, thus with α ≈ 1.119 > 1. However, the optimal exponent α and the precise best anytime rate remain unresolved; known upper bounds (around T^{−1.119}) do not match the known information-theoretic limit (around T^{−2} from accelerated methods), so the problem is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Anytime Acceleration of Gradient Descent
status_evidence.snippet: stepsize schedule that allows gradient descent to achieve convergence guarantees of O(T^{-1.119}) for any stopping time T
status_evidence.claim: An explicit silver-ratio-based stepsize sequence achieves an anytime rate with exponent α ≈ 1.119 > 1, affirmatively answering the existence question.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Anytime Convergence Rate of Gradient Descent
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem posed at COLT 2024 asking for the best anytime convergence rate of GD on smooth convex functions.
status_evidence.claim: The original problem was posed as an open problem at COLT 2024.

status_evidence.title: Acceleration by stepsize hedging: Silver Stepsize Schedule
status_evidence.snippet: Silver stepsize schedule yields accelerated convergence for smooth convex optimization.
status_evidence.claim: Silver-ratio stepsize schedules provide acceleration beyond the classical O(1/T) rate, supporting partial resolution of the problem.
